justification: Removes a customer-facing feature from the granny-flat ineligible result: the 'Eligible properties nearby' block, its API route and its tests. Standard rather than critical because removal is the safe direction — no claim is added, no stored data changes, and no code path can now serve a wrong result from it. It is not minor: it deletes a served surface and a public endpoint.

falsifiable_check.claim: Nothing still references the removed endpoint or component, and no other feature depended on them.
falsifiable_check.fails_when: Any remaining source file references /api/reports/granny-flat/nearby, NearbyEligible, or NearbyResult; or tsc/jest regress.
falsifiable_check.how_checked: grep for 'granny-flat/nearby', 'NearbyEligible', 'NearbyResult' and 'selectedLat|selectedLng' across frontend-nextjs; npx tsc --noEmit; npx jest.
falsifiable_check.command: grep -rn 'granny-flat/nearby\|NearbyEligible\|electedLat' frontend-nextjs --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx | grep -v node_modules   &&   cd frontend-nextjs && npx tsc --noEmit && npx jest
falsifiable_check.result: PASSED. 0 references remain. tsc 0 errors. jest 78 suites / 1025 tests pass (down 10 = the deleted route's own tests). The similarly-named nearby_secondary_dwelling_count in GrannyFlatTool.tsx is a DA-approval count from a different pipeline and is deliberately untouched.

pre_impl.existing_data: The endpoint filtered granny_flat_reports on confidence='high' AND granny_flat_buildable=true. That is 11 rows, spread over 9 postcodes, with one address (12 Selby Place Blacktown) stored three times so it would have listed the same property up to three times. Measured 2026-08-06: only 3 of 87 stored addresses have any such row within the 1km radius, so the block returned empty for 97% of addresses.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: A mid-review grep suggested selectedLat/selectedLng were never set, which would have made the block unreachable dead code. That was wrong — the grep under-reported; setSelectedLat(lat) is called at page.tsx:462 on address selection, so the block did render. Re-verified against origin/main before acting; the removal is justified on purpose and liability, not on it being dead.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Pure deletion. The component, its route and its test file are removed; selectedLat/selectedLng state became write-only as a result of the deletion and is removed with it, per the cleanup rule. No replacement is added — the ineligible result now goes straight from the notify-me block to the cross-sell cards.

functions: N/A — deletion only, no new or changed functions.
values: N/A — no values are read or written by this change.
queries: N/A — the only query in the change is the one being deleted.

break_it.scenario: Another surface still calls /api/reports/granny-flat/nearby after the route file is deleted, so a live page starts issuing requests that now 404.
break_it.what_happens: The calling page would silently render an empty section forever, because the original component swallowed fetch errors with a bare catch and a graceful empty state — the failure would be invisible rather than loud.
break_it.how: Grepped the whole frontend for 'granny-flat/nearby' after deletion: zero references. The only caller was the component removed in the same commit.
break_it.repro: grep -rn 'granny-flat/nearby' frontend-nextjs --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx | grep -v node_modules   (expect no output)

break_it.scenario: The deletion catches the unrelated nearby_secondary_dwelling_count feature in GrannyFlatTool.tsx, which shares the word 'nearby'.
break_it.what_happens: A genuine, separately-sourced count of nearby secondary dwelling APPROVALS from DA data would vanish from the tool, removing real information rather than the manufactured comparables.
break_it.how: Each of the four other files matching 'nearby' was opened and classified before deleting anything: two are navigation copy about nearby councils, and GrannyFlatTool's nearby_secondary_dwelling_count is DA-approval data from a different pipeline. All four are untouched and their tests still pass.

break_it.scenario: selectedLat/selectedLng are left in place after their only reader is deleted, or are removed too aggressively and break address selection.
break_it.what_happens: Left in, they are write-only state that a later reader could resurrect and re-point at a removed feature. Removed carelessly, the onSelect handler at page.tsx:462 loses sibling setters in the same arrow body and address selection stops recording the address or postcode.
break_it.how: Removed by exact-string replacement of only the selectedLat/selectedLng fragments, leaving setAddress/setPostcode and the other reset setters in the same handlers intact. Verified by 0 remaining references, tsc 0 errors, and the full jest suite passing.
break_it.repro: grep -n 'electedLat\|electedLng' frontend-nextjs/app/reports/granny-flat/page.tsx   (expect no output), then npx tsc --noEmit

post_merge.db_reset: None. No migration and no writes. The 11 rows the endpoint used to select are untouched and keep their stored values.
post_merge.secrets: None added, changed or removed by this change.
post_merge.other_repo: None. The endpoint had no external caller; it was fetched only from the page in this repo.
post_merge.manual_verify: Load a granny-flat result for an ineligible address and confirm the 'Eligible properties nearby' teal block no longer appears, and that the notify-me block and cross-sell cards still render in order.
